newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 96/97 soybean harvest 91 pct sold - Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 96/97 soybean harvest 91 pct sold - Safras.

text.p: Brazilian farmers had sold 91 percent of the total expected 1996/97 soybean crop by the week ending July 31, independent consultant Safras e Mercado said.

This compared with 85 percent at the same stage in 1996, which was also the average over the last five years, Safras said. Assuming a total harvest of 26.02 million tonnes, this meant there were 2.4 million tonnes left to be sold.
A sharp drop in both international and domestic prices in early July prompted some nervous producers to sell, even though domestic prices were showing signs of independent strength, Safras noted.
But domestic prices recovered after the scare of the first 10 days, ending the month up 13 to 19 percent on the same period last year.

The question now was what would happen to the domestic market during the next six months, given that there will be practically no domestic soybean offer until the new harvest comes on stream in February 1998, Safras said.
The market would now remain focused on the weather in the U.S., crucial towards determining the size of the crop there.

"On the domestic front, what will be observed from now is an elasticity in prices, much less on the downside than on the upside," it said. In effect, domestic prices will accompany rises on the Chicago commodities futures exchange but not drops.
